concept.name: Continuation
concept.definition: The resumption of the prevailing trend after a pause, pullback, or consolidation. In classical chart analysis, continuation is the default expectation associated with congestion patterns and mid-trend gaps — a probabilistic heuristic, not a law.
concept.intuition: The trend catches its breath and then keeps going in the same direction.
concept.mechanics: Identified when a counter-move or sideways congestion resolves with a break in the direction of the prior trend — e.g., a consolidation range breaking with the trend, or a runaway (continuation) gap appearing mid-trend on rising volume.
concept.failure_modes: Not every pause continues the trend — some consolidations are distribution or accumulation that precede reversals, so continuation assumptions fail at trend turning points.
concept.misconceptions: That a pause in a trend guarantees continuation; continuation is the base-rate expectation, but each individual congestion can resolve either way.
concept.example: A stock trending up pauses in a two-week sideways range, then gaps higher on increased volume — a continuation resolution of the congestion.
